messages:
maya-cs: FYI I drafted a compact 'risk-tiered priming' handoff for onboarding -> enablement -> expansion. idea is to link account health + renewal risk to specific priming patterns (cache, batch, stream) so support/eng follow the same playbook

sam-ce: love the idea. can you paste the short checklist here? easier to iterate in-thread.

maya-cs: sure — kept to one pager. TL;DR: tag customer as GREEN/YELLOW/RED on kickoff. each tag maps to priming budget, prefill TTL, streaming policy, and feedback cadence.

maya-cs: CHECKLIST (copyable):
```
- Tag account: GREEN | YELLOW | RED
- Priming budget: GREEN=low, YELLOW=medium, RED=high
- Prefill TTL: GREEN=24h, YELLOW=72h, RED=7d
- Streaming policy: GREEN=optional, YELLOW=recommended, RED=required with fallback to short-generate
- Batching: GREEN=batch=0.5s, YELLOW=1s, RED=0.25s (aggressive batching + warm pools)
- Eval sampling: GREEN=1/day, YELLOW=10/day, RED=100/day
- Feedback capture: attach triage form on any model mismatch for YELLOW/RED
```

rachel-cs-lead: nice. can we add a quick triage script for SRE/eng to run on go-live if latency spikes?

ash-eng: (ash-eng) here's a minimal probe we use in eng-runtime. run on suspected warmup / cache-miss events:
```
curl -s -X POST https://probe.redwood.internal/ping -d '{"account":"<acct>","probe":"prefill-check"}' | jq .status
# expected: {"status":"ok","warm_pool":true,"avg_lat_ms":85}
```

maya-cs: perfect — I'll paste that into the handoff doc. also adding a quick scoring rule: if avg_lat_ms > 250ms during 3 consecutive probes -> escalate to eng-sre + open a quick postmortem card.

jorge-data: two quick asks from telemetry side: 1) tag events emitted when priming has finished (prefill_done) 2) capture sample prompts and model reply hashes for RED/YELLOW for 72h window so we can run regressions. we can auto-create a daily digest to surface anomalies.

maya-cs: added. i'll make the digest a daily DM to the account owner and a weekly summary to the AE/CSM.

sam-ce: how do we capture customer feedback efficiently? we want lightweight but structured.

maya-cs: we proposed a one-click triage widget at the top of the app for RED/YELLOW accounts ("answer was wrong/irrelevant/slow"). it triggers a short form with tags and auto-attaches last 3 prompts+responses. minimal friction.

rachel-cs-lead: routing: all RED tickets create a high-priority support case and notify #eng-oncall; YELLOW creates a regular ticket routed to CSM + solutions eng. GREEN is self-serve.

ash-eng: two engineering notes on batching/cache: 1) aggressive batching helps throughput but increases tail latency for single-user flows. for RED accounts we prefer dedicated warm pools. 2) KV cache TTLs should match prefill TTLs above and be adjustable per-account via flag.

maya-cs: i'll include these as implementation constraints in the runbook. also adding a fallback policy: if streaming fails, fall back to short-generate with a one-line apology and a telemetry tag 'fallback_short_gen'.

ops-bot: deploy:runbook/risk-tiered-priming v1.0 deployed by maya-cs at 2026-03-23T15:12Z :white_check_mark:

sam-ce: small proposal: include an onboarding gating checklist — require small successful live queries (p95 latency < 300ms for 50 samples) before marking as GREEN. otherwise default to YELLOW until warmed.

maya-cs: added gating criteria. will test with the next pilot. anyone want owner for the pilot?

rachel-cs-lead: i can own pilot scheduling and AE outreach. maya, sam, jorge — we should sync for data hooks.

maya-cs: thanks. action items: 1) maya: update doc with ash probe + gating (today) 2) jorge: set up digest pipeline (48h) 3) rachel: schedule pilot outreach and kickoff (EOW) 4) ash: confirm probe endpoint auth + playbook for oncall (EOD)

sam-ce: thumbs up. this feels distinct enough from our existing playbooks (more signal-driven and triage-focused). ship when ready. :thumbsup:

maya-cs: will post final one-pager in docs channel and link in CSM playbook after pilot. thanks all.
